A0AAQ4DMB8.family: Ornithine cyclodeaminase/mu-crystallin family (PF02423); IPR003462, IPR023401 (N-terminal), IPR036291 (NAD(P)-binding domain superfamily)
A0AAQ4DMB8.oligomeric_evidence: UniProt SUBUNIT text for this accession explicitly states 'Homodimer. Binds the thyroid hormone triiodothyronine (T3); T3 binding inhibits enzymatic activity.' Confirmed independently by PDB biological assembly of the mouse ortholog (PDB 4BVA, 4BV9, 4BV8: 'Homo 2-mer - A2', Cyclic C2 symmetry).
A0AAQ4DMB8.binding_site_location: NADPH and T3-hormone binding pocket is INTRA-subunit: each monomer of the dimer has its own complete binding pocket (Rossmann-like NAD(P)-binding fold + C-terminal domain forming the T3 cavity). The dimer interface exists but does not complete the ligand pocket the way GST's H-site does. Mouse mu-crystallin PDB 4BVA (NADPH+T3 bound) shows T3 binding 'mainly through hydrophobic interactions' within one subunit's pocket; NADPH binding induces a conformational change that pre-organizes the T3 pocket (allosteric coupling between the two ligands, still within the same subunit).
A0AAQ4DMB8.site_residues_known: Not extracted to residue-number precision in the sources reviewed here (would require inspecting the 4BVA coordinate file/paper directly). The fold and pocket-forming secondary structure elements are described (NAD(P)-binding Rossmann domain + T3 pocket), but no catalytic-triad-style motif is quoted here.
A0AAQ4DMB8.characterized_relatives: Mouse Mu-crystallin (CRYM), PDB 4BV8 (apo), 4BV9 (NADPH-bound), 4BVA (NADPH + T3 thyroid-hormone bound) — Borel F et al., FEBS J 2014 (PMID 24467707). This is a directly ligand-bound, high-identity mammalian ortholog with the exact EC activities (1.5.1.1/1.5.1.25) matching the tick UniProt annotation, and is the single strongest structural template found in this chunk.
A0AAQ4DMB8.chembl_target: UNKNOWN — not verified in this pass. Human CRYM is studied as a T3-sequestration protein but no ChEMBL target ID was confirmed via search.
A0AAQ4DMB8.druggability_note: Well-defined intra-subunit NADPH+T3 pocket transferable by homology from mouse CRYM (PDB 4BVA). Good candidate for direct pocket transfer rather than blind fpocket prediction — the ligand-bound mouse structure can be superposed onto the tick AlphaFold model to seed the docking box.

Q2Q443.family: Cytosolic glutathione S-transferase (GST) superfamily; IPR004045 (GST N-terminal, thioredoxin-fold), IPR010987/IPR036282 (GST C-terminal, all-alpha), IPR040079 (GST family). Pfam PF02798 (GST_N).
Q2Q443.oligomeric_evidence: UniProt SUBUNIT field for THIS accession explicitly states 'Homodimer' — direct evidence, not inference. Consistent with essentially universal cytosolic-GST biology (mu/alpha/pi/theta/delta/epsilon classes are all obligate homo- or hetero-dimers).
Q2Q443.binding_site_location: INTER-subunit for the H-site, INTRA-subunit for the G-site (GSH-binding site). This is the decisive point for the pipeline's pocket-selection problem: the G-site (glutathione binding) sits mostly within the N-terminal thioredoxin-fold domain of one subunit, but the H-site (hydrophobic electrophile-binding site) is completed by loops donated from the neighboring subunit's C-terminal domain — a single-subunit fpocket run will find at most half the real pocket. Directly demonstrated for a congeneric tick GST: cryo/MD study of Rhipicephalus (Boophilus) microplus GST (RmGST, mu-class) states 'the binding of both GSH and GTX requires cooperation between subunits' (PMC9655991).
Q2Q443.site_residues_known: For the closely related tick ortholog RmGST (mu-class, MD/homology-modeled against templates 1XW6 and 1GSU): G-site residues W8, R43, W46, K50, N59, L60, Q72, S73; catalytic Tyr stabilizes the GSH thiolate — 'the hydroxyl group of Y7 was in close proximity to a sulfur atom (S) on GSH' (Y7/Y116 in RmGST numbering, analogous to Y6/Y115 in mammalian mu-class GSTs). NOTE: these residue numbers are from RmGST, a homolog, not from Q2Q443 itself — sequence numbering will differ; use for motif/role transfer only, not literal residue mapping without an alignment.
Q2Q443.characterized_relatives: No PDB structure exists for Q2Q443 or for RmGST itself (RmGST paper used homology modeling, not crystallography). However, the cytosolic GST fold is one of the best-characterized enzyme folds in structural biology generally, with hundreds of ligand-bound (GSH- and S-alkylglutathione-bound) ligand structures across classes — the RmGST paper's own templates were PDB 1XW6 (GSH-bound GST) and 1GSU (S-hexylglutathione-bound GST). Any of these generic GSH/S-alkylglutathione-bound cytosolic GST structures (mu/alpha class) is a usable homology template for placing the G-site + H-site as a dimer-interface pocket, once class is confirmed by sequence alignment.
Q2Q443.chembl_target: GST superfamily is broadly represented in ChEMBL as a drug/detox target class (e.g., human GSTM1/GSTP1 — search via Pharos confirmed GSTM1/M2/M3/M4 entries exist) but a specific verified ChEMBL target ID for this insect/tick GST or its closest human paralog was not confirmed in this pass — reported as UNKNOWN rather than guessed.
Q2Q443.druggability_note: GSTs are validated small-molecule targets in both pharma (isoform-selective GST inhibitors exist) and acaricide/insecticide contexts (GST overexpression is a major xenobiotic-resistance mechanism in ticks, so a GST inhibitor could double as a resistance-breaker). CRITICAL FOR THE PIPELINE: because the H-site is inter-subunit, docking against a monomeric AlphaFold model with an fpocket-picked intra-subunit-only site is very likely to miss or mis-shape the true binding site. Recommend building/using a homodimer model (AlphaFold-Multimer or symmetric docking of two copies) before pocket definition for this and any other GST-family target discovered later.
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9655991/ (Observing How Glutathione and S-Hexyl Glutathione Bind to GST from Rhipicephalus (Boophilus) microplus)

Q06EX9.family: MIP/Aquaporin superfamily; IPR000425 (Major intrinsic protein), IPR023271 (Aquaporin-like), IPR050363 (MIP/Aquaporin family). Pfam PF00230. UniProt SIMILARITY: 'Belongs to the MIP/aquaporin (TC 1.A.8) family.'
Q06EX9.oligomeric_evidence: Not stated in this accession's own UniProt SUBUNIT field (none present), but tetrameric assembly is universal, structurally invariant family convention for the MIP/aquaporin superfamily across all kingdoms (every solved AQP/aquaglyceroporin structure — human AQP1/AQP4/AQP5, E. coli GlpF, plant SoPIP2 — is a homotetramer in the membrane). Treat as high-confidence by family convention even though not directly stated for this accession; would be strengthened by an AlphaFold-Multimer tetramer build.
Q06EX9.binding_site_location: TWO DISTINCT SITES — this is exactly the question flagged as important. (1) The functional water/glycerol conduction pore is INTRA-subunit: each of the 4 monomers folds into the classic 'hourglass' 6-TM-helix fold with its own complete pore, selectivity filter, and NPA (Asn-Pro-Ala) motif pair — so each subunit is independently functional, and single-subunit modeling is legitimate for THIS site. (2) A separate, structurally distinct 'central pore' running down the 4-fold symmetry axis is INTER-subunit by definition — it is built from contributions of all four monomers and does not exist in a monomer at all. Its physiological role is debated/still-researched but literature links it to gas permeation (CO2, NH3, possibly NO) in some aquaporins, not water/glycerol transport. Practical implication: if the pipeline's interest is the canonical aquaglyceroporin transport function (most likely, given the annotated role in anhydrobiosis/osmolyte handling), monomer-based pocket picking at the conserved NPA/ar-R constriction is defensible; if interest is a hypothetical gas-conduction inhibitor, a tetramer build is required since that pore doesn't exist in a monomer.
Q06EX9.site_residues_known: Yes, at the family level: the two NPA (Asn-Pro-Ala) boxes are the single most conserved motif in the entire MIP/aquaporin superfamily, forming the pore's electrostatic barrier at the vestibule center; the aromatic/Arginine (ar/R) selectivity filter near the extracellular vestibule additionally tunes water-vs-glycerol/solute selectivity (glycerol-permeable aquaglyceroporins have a wider, more hydrophobic ar/R filter than strict water channels). Exact residue numbers were not extracted for Q06EX9 specifically in this pass (would need the AlphaFold model + a Pfam PF00230 HMM alignment to localize the two NPA boxes precisely in this sequence).
Q06EX9.characterized_relatives: No tick-specific aquaporin PDB structure identified. Generic ligand/inhibitor-free family structures exist and are usable homology templates for pore geometry: human AQP1 (1FQY, 1J4N), bacterial glycerol facilitator GlpF (1FX8, ligand/glycerol-bound), plant SoPIP2;1 (spinach, gated aquaporin, 2B5F). None found here are tick-specific, so pocket transfer would rely on the conserved fold rather than a close identity match.
Q06EX9.chembl_target: UNKNOWN — small-molecule aquaporin inhibitors are an active but immature area (e.g., TGN-020 for AQP4); no ChEMBL ID confirmed for an aquaglyceroporin/AQP9-class target in this pass.
Q06EX9.druggability_note: Aquaporins are traditionally considered a difficult druggable class (shallow, highly conserved, mostly water-filled pores with few good small-molecule anchor points), but aquaglyceroporins are somewhat more tractable than strict water channels because their wider ar/R filter accommodates larger solutes/inhibitors. Given anhydrobiosis-related function noted in the local annotation, an aquaglyceroporin inhibitor is mechanistically attractive (disrupt water/osmolyte balance in the unfed tick) even if medicinal-chemistry tractability is moderate.
sources: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/7/11/209 (Aquaporins: More Than Functional Monomers in a Tetrameric Arrangement)

B7P2S1.provenance_note: DELETED from UniProt in release 2026_01 (confirmed: live REST query for B7P2S1 returned no entry). Per config.py TARGET_PROVENANCE this is Tier 3 with anchor EMBL_CON:EEC00893 (UPI00018E8FF9). Family/domain data below comes from the LOCAL cached final_targets.json record, captured before deletion, not from a live re-verification.
B7P2S1.family: Nuclear hormone receptor, NR1 subfamily; IPR000536 (NHR ligand-binding domain), IPR001628 (Zinc finger, NHR-type), IPR001723 (Nuclear hormone receptor family), IPR013088/IPR035500 (Zn-finger/NHR-LBD superfamilies), IPR050234 (Nuclear hormone receptor family NR1 subfamily).
B7P2S1.family_confidence: high (from cached InterPro annotation; not independently re-verified live because the UniProt entry is gone)
B7P2S1.oligomeric_state: COMPLEX (obligate heterodimer, by strong family convention)
B7P2S1.oligomeric_evidence: Not directly stated for this specific (now-deleted) accession. Family convention: arthropod NR1-subfamily nuclear receptors (this subfamily includes the ecdysone-receptor-associated and xenobiotic-sensing receptors, e.g. HR96) function as ligand-activated transcription factors, and the best-characterized arthropod steroid receptor system (the ecdysone receptor EcR, also NR1 clan) is an obligate heterodimer with the RXR ortholog Ultraspiracle (USP, NR2B4) — DNA binding and often ligand response require the partner subunit. Whether B7P2S1 itself heterodimerizes with a USP/RXR-type partner (like A0A4D5RYT8 in this same chunk) or is a different NR1 receptor with its own dimerization behavior is UNKNOWN without direct evidence.
B7P2S1.binding_site_location: By universal nuclear-receptor architecture, the ligand-binding pocket is INTRA-subunit: a single hydrophobic cavity within the C-terminal ligand-binding domain (LBD) of ONE subunit, formed by helices 3, 5, 6, 7 and 11 of the canonical NR-LBD fold (this exact helix-numbering description is used for the homologous insect xenobiotic receptor HR96, itself modeled on the vertebrate LXR-beta template PDB 4NQA). The DNA-binding zinc-finger domain is separate and N-terminal. Heterodimerization (if it occurs, see above) affects transcriptional output/partner recruitment but does not itself complete the ligand pocket the way GST's H-site does — so a monomeric LBD model is a defensible unit for docking, PROVIDED the correct domain (LBD, not the zinc-finger DBD) is isolated and the pocket helices are correctly identified rather than left to naive whole-protein fpocket, since NR1 proteins have two structurally and functionally unrelated domains (DBD zinc-finger + LBD) and fpocket run on the full-length AlphaFold model could easily pick a spurious pocket in the linker or DBD.
B7P2S1.site_residues_known: Not extracted to residue-number precision for B7P2S1. The general helix framework (H3/H5/H6/H7/H11 lining the pocket) is a strong, transferable family fact for any NR1/NR2 LBD.
B7P2S1.characterized_relatives: No direct tick or arthropod NR1 ligand-bound structure identified for this specific receptor. The most relevant published homology-modeling precedent is the mite/spider-mite xenobiotic receptor TcHR96h (Tetranychus cinnabarinus), modeled on vertebrate LXR-beta (PDB 4NQA) — same NR1 clan reasoning applicable here. Generic vertebrate NR1-family ligand-bound LBD structures usable as fold templates: RORγt LBD + SRC2 peptide (PDB 5VB3), orphan NR2E3/PNR LBD (PDB 4LOG). None are tick-specific.
B7P2S1.chembl_target: UNKNOWN for this specific receptor. The broader nuclear-receptor superfamily (including RORγt) is heavily represented in ChEMBL, but no ID specific to this tick NR1 ortholog was found or should be assumed.
B7P2S1.druggability_note: Nuclear receptor LBDs are among the most historically druggable pocket classes (deep, well-defined hydrophobic cavities, precedented by agonists/antagonists across the whole superfamily). If this receptor is confirmed to be the arthropod ecdysone-pathway type, it sits in the same target class as diacylhydrazine insecticides (tebufenozide etc.) which are validated commercial acaricide/insecticide chemotypes acting on this exact receptor family (see also B7P2S1's project sibling B7PY20, an NHR already flagged in this project's own notes as a diacylhydrazine-chemotype hit).

A0A4D5RYT8.provenance_note: DELETED from UniProt in release 2026_01 (confirmed: live REST query returned nothing). Per config.py TARGET_PROVENANCE this is Tier 4 with anchor EMBL_TSA:MOY42500 (UPI0010C71910). Family/domain data below comes from the LOCAL cached final_targets.json record.
A0A4D5RYT8.family: Nuclear hormone receptor, NR2 subfamily / Retinoid X receptor-HNF4 family; IPR000003 (RXR/HNF4 family), IPR000536 (NHR-LBD), IPR001628 (Zn-finger NHR-type), IPR001723 (NHR family), IPR013088/IPR035500 (superfamilies), IPR049635 (HNF4 LBD), IPR049636 (HNF4-like DBD), IPR050274 (NHR family NR2 subfamily).
A0A4D5RYT8.family_confidence: high (from cached InterPro annotation; the specific IPR049635/49636 HNF4-ligand-binding-domain hits are a strong, specific signal, not just generic NHR)
A0A4D5RYT8.oligomeric_state: COMPLEX (dimer, by strong family convention — either homodimer as HNF4 does, or heterodimer if functioning as the arthropod RXR ortholog USP)
A0A4D5RYT8.oligomeric_evidence: Not directly stated for this (now-deleted) accession. Two family precedents both point to dimerization: (a) human HNF4α functions as an obligate homodimer bound to DNA — PDB 4IQR is explicitly 'the multidomain human HNF-4α homodimer bound to its DNA response element'; (b) if this receptor is instead the arthropod RXR ortholog (Ultraspiracle/USP, NR2B4 clan, same broad IPR000003 family), it is the obligate heterodimer partner of the ecdysone receptor EcR. Which of the two functional roles applies to A0A4D5RYT8 specifically is UNKNOWN without a phylogenetic/sequence-identity check against human HNF4A vs. arthropod USP — both hit the same top-level InterPro family.
A0A4D5RYT8.binding_site_location: INTRA-subunit. The HNF4 LBD binds long-chain fatty acids constitutively within a single hydrophobic channel inside one subunit's LBD: 'the carboxylic acid headgroup of the fatty acid ion pairs with the guanidinium group of Arg226 at one end of the ligand binding pocket, while the aliphatic chain fills a long, narrow channel lined with hydrophobic residues' (human HNF4γ LBD, PDB 1LV2; homodimer-on-DNA context in 4IQR). If instead this is a USP/RXR-type ortholog, note the caution flagged in this project's own CLAUDE.md history: arthropod USP has, in several lineages, LOST a functional ligand-binding pocket (Hemiptera, Coleoptera) or acquired an unusual phospholipid-filled pocket (Mecopterida) — so 'has a druggable LBD pocket' cannot be assumed for the USP interpretation without direct evidence for this receptor.
A0A4D5RYT8.site_residues_known: For the HNF4 interpretation: Arg226 (fatty-acid carboxylate anchor) is a directly quoted, named residue from the human HNF4γ structure (PDB 1LV2) — high-confidence motif, but HNF4γ numbering, not this tick sequence's numbering; needs alignment before literal transfer.
A0A4D5RYT8.characterized_relatives: Human HNF4α, PDB 4IQR (2.9 Å, multidomain homodimer bound to DNA response element + fatty-acid ligand + coactivator peptide) and PDB 1M7W (HNF4α LBD with bound fatty acid); human HNF4γ, PDB 1LV2 (LBD with endogenous fatty acid, Arg226 anchor). These are directly ligand-bound structures and, if sequence identity to A0A4D5RYT8 is confirmed to be closer to HNF4 than to arthropod USP, are strong transferable templates.
A0A4D5RYT8.chembl_target: Human HNF4A has a confirmed ChEMBL single-protein target entry: CHEMBL5398 (Homo sapiens, Hepatocyte nuclear factor 4-alpha). Relevance to this tick receptor depends on confirming the HNF4-vs-USP identity question above.
A0A4D5RYT8.druggability_note: If HNF4-like: constitutively fatty-acid-occupied LBD pocket is a real, structurally validated small-molecule pocket (agonists/antagonists exist for human HNF4A in the oncology/MODY-diabetes literature). If USP-like: druggability is uncertain and lineage-dependent per the pocket-loss/pocket-gain literature above — this ambiguity should be resolved (sequence-based, e.g. a quick BLAST of this sequence against human HNF4A vs. Drosophila/Ixodes USP) before committing docking effort here.

B7SP48.family: Papain-like cysteine peptidase, clan CA, family C1A (cathepsin-like); IPR000668, IPR013128, IPR038765. Pfam PF00112 (Peptidase_C1). MEROPS C01.160.
B7SP48.oligomeric_evidence: Family convention: C1A papain-family cysteine proteases (cathepsins B/L/K/S and their tick midgut orthologs) are functional monomers — no SUBUNIT oligomer text in UniProt and no dimerization documented for this family broadly; the papain fold itself is a self-contained catalytic unit.
B7SP48.binding_site_location: INTRA-subunit. Classic papain fold: a cleft between two lobes (one mostly alpha-helical, one mostly beta-sheet) of a SINGLE polypeptide, with the Cys-His-Asn catalytic triad at the cleft base. No inter-subunit contribution — this family is one of the 'easy' cases for the pipeline's monomer-based fpocket approach, in contrast to GST.
B7SP48.site_residues_known: Yes, at family level, with high confidence: the papain-family catalytic triad is Cys25-His159-Asn175 in papain numbering (classic textbook motif); InterPro entries explicitly separate 'cysteine active site' (IPR000169), 'histidine active site' (IPR025660) and 'asparagine active site' (IPR025661) as conserved sub-signatures of this same superfamily (seen in the closely related A7LJ78 entry, same clan). A propeptide (I29 inhibitor domain, PF08246) covers the active site in the zymogen form and must be removed/modeled as cleaved for docking.
B7SP48.characterized_relatives: No PDB structure specific to B7SP48. The C1A/papain family overall is one of the most heavily structurally characterized protease families in the PDB, with abundant ligand(inhibitor)-bound structures for human cathepsins B, L, K, S (covalent and non-covalent inhibitors, e.g. E-64 class) and numerous parasite/tick orthologs. A congeneric tick cathepsin (Rhipicephalus microplus cathepsin, and the sibling accessions A7LJ78/B7SP44 in this same chunk) provide close within-genus homology templates once a specific PDB ID is picked by BLAST against the PDB.
B7SP48.chembl_target: Cathepsin family broadly present in ChEMBL; general-family entries confirmed (not this specific tick ortholog): human Cathepsin L (CHEMBL3837 among several ChEMBL cathepsin-L records), human Cathepsin B (CHEMBL4072), human Cathepsin K (CHEMBL268), human Cathepsin S (CHEMBL2954). Choose the correct paralog match by sequence identity before using any specific one as a bioactivity reference.
B7SP48.druggability_note: One of the best-precedented druggable families in this entire chunk. Cysteine cathepsins are validated drug targets in human medicine (osteoporosis, cancer) and specifically implicated in tick blood-meal digestion (midgut cysteine proteinases), making this a mechanistically attractive acaricide target class independent of the pocket-location question that motivated this research pass.

A7LJ78.family: Papain-like cysteine peptidase, clan CA, family C1A; IPR000169 (Cys active site), IPR000668, IPR013128, IPR025660 (His active site), IPR025661 (Asn active site), IPR038765, IPR039417. Pfam PF00112, PF08246.
A7LJ78.oligomeric_evidence: Family convention (see B7SP48 entry, same family) — no SUBUNIT oligomer text; papain-fold cysteine proteases are self-contained monomeric catalytic units.
A7LJ78.binding_site_location: INTRA-subunit — classic papain-fold active-site cleft within a single chain (see B7SP48 for full description; identical family reasoning applies).
A7LJ78.site_residues_known: Yes: papain-family catalytic triad Cys-His-Asn (textbook Cys25/His159/Asn175 papain numbering); this accession explicitly carries the three separate InterPro 'active site' sub-signatures for all three catalytic residues (IPR000169/IPR025660/IPR025661), which is unusually complete confirmation compared to most family members annotated in this chunk.
A7LJ78.characterized_relatives: Same family-level relatives as B7SP48 (human cathepsin L/B/K/S ligand-bound structures; sibling tick paralogs B7SP44, B7SP48 in this chunk). No PDB structure specific to A7LJ78 itself.
A7LJ78.chembl_target: Human Cathepsin L, ChEMBL target CHEMBL3837 (also CHEMBL2113, CHEMBL2305 — multiple ChEMBL records exist for cathepsin L across sources); confirm paralog match by sequence identity before use.
A7LJ78.druggability_note: Same strong druggability case as B7SP48 — this accession additionally has all three catalytic-triad active-site InterPro signatures independently confirmed, making it one of the highest-confidence family assignments in the whole chunk.

B7SP44.name_local: Putative cathepsin B-like cysteine protease form 1 (fragment)
B7SP44.family: Papain-like cysteine peptidase, clan CA, family C1A, cathepsin-B-like subfamily; IPR000668, IPR013128, IPR038765. Pfam PF00112. CDD cd02620 (Peptidase_C1A_CathepsinB) — explicit cathepsin-B sub-classification, stronger than a generic C1A hit.
B7SP44.oligomeric_evidence: Family convention (papain-fold proteases are monomeric catalytic units); no contrary SUBUNIT annotation present. NOTE: mammalian cathepsin B specifically has a distinctive 'occluding loop' that can partially block the active-site cleft and confers dipeptidyl-carboxypeptidase activity in addition to endopeptidase activity — this is an intra-chain structural feature, not an oligomerization event, but worth flagging since it changes pocket shape versus cathepsin L.
B7SP44.binding_site_location: INTRA-subunit papain-fold active-site cleft (see B7SP48). For the cathepsin-B subtype specifically, expect the occluding loop near the C-terminal end of the cleft to partially cap one side of the pocket in the mature enzyme — relevant if using a cathepsin-L-like homology template instead of a true cathepsin-B template for pocket shape.
B7SP44.site_residues_known: Papain-family Cys-His-Asn catalytic triad (family-level, high confidence); this accession's own IPR000668 hit covers only the C-terminal His/Asn-bearing region explicitly (the N-terminal Cys active-site sub-signature IPR000169 was not returned for this specific accession in the InterPro query, unlike A7LJ78 — may reflect an incomplete/fragment sequence, consistent with the record being flagged as a fragment).
B7SP44.characterized_relatives: Human Cathepsin B is one of the most thoroughly ligand-bound-structure-characterized cysteine proteases in the PDB (numerous inhibitor complexes). No PDB structure specific to B7SP44 itself; sibling tick paralogs A7LJ78/B7SP48 in this chunk are close within-genus references.
B7SP44.chembl_target: Human Cathepsin B, ChEMBL target CHEMBL4072 confirmed via direct search (Homo sapiens, single protein, EC 3.4.22.1).
B7SP44.druggability_note: Same strong C1A-family druggability case as A7LJ78/B7SP48, with the added note that cathepsin-B-type pockets have a partially occluded cleft (occluding loop) that should be reflected in box/pocket definition rather than borrowing a cathepsin-L pocket shape uncritically.

A0A0C9R1D7.family: PICK1-type PDZ+BAR(Arfaptin-homology) domain scaffold protein; IPR001478/IPR036034 (PDZ domain/superfamily), IPR010504 (Arfaptin homology/AH domain), IPR027267 (AH/BAR domain superfamily), IPR030798 (Arfaptin family). Pfam PF00595/PF13180 (PDZ), PF06456 (Arfaptin-like).
A0A0C9R1D7.oligomeric_evidence: UniProt SUBUNIT field for THIS accession explicitly states 'Functions as monomer and homodimer' — direct evidence. This matches human PICK1 biology, where the BAR (Arfaptin-homology) domain forms an obligate crescent-shaped homodimer (a structural requirement of essentially all BAR-domain proteins), while the PDZ domain can act as a largely independent module.
A0A0C9R1D7.binding_site_location: Two functionally distinct, both largely INTRA-domain sites, though the full-length protein assembles as a dimer via the BAR domain: (1) the PDZ domain has a canonical INTRA-subunit peptide-binding groove (binds C-terminal tails of partner proteins, e.g. AMPA receptor GluA2) plus a separate lipid-membrane-binding surface stabilized by a 'Cys-Pro-Cys' redox motif located away from the peptide groove — human PICK1 PDZ was crystallized as an oxidized DIMER in complex with the GluR2 C-tail peptide (PDB 3HPK), where a disulfide bond forms an inter-subunit contact that is regulatory (redox-sensing) rather than a shared catalytic/ligand pocket. (2) The BAR domain forms the classic crescent-shaped, curvature-sensing homodimer (inter-subunit by definition, since a BAR domain dimer only exists as two chains together), and the PDZ domain has been shown to dock into the concave face of this BAR dimer intramolecularly, autoinhibiting it.
A0A0C9R1D7.site_residues_known: Not extracted to residue-number precision here beyond the named 'Cys-Pro-Cys' (CPC) motif in the PDZ domain (redox/lipid-sensing, located away from the peptide-binding groove).
A0A0C9R1D7.characterized_relatives: Human PICK1 PDZ domain, PDB 3HPK (oxidized dimeric PDZ + GluR2 C-tail peptide — directly ligand/peptide-bound). A specific small-molecule PDZ-groove antagonist chemical probe, BIO124, and a peptide inhibitor (Tat-P4-(C5)2, ~2 nM) are both documented in the medicinal-chemistry literature (see Expert Opin Drug Discov review, 2026, doi:10.1080/14728222.2026.2625095), indicating this exact pocket class has been actively drugged in the human ortholog.
A0A0C9R1D7.chembl_target: UNKNOWN — not verified for human PICK1 (PRKCABP) in this pass despite the existence of published chemical probes; do not assume a ChEMBL ID without checking.
A0A0C9R1D7.druggability_note: The PDZ peptide-binding groove is a validated, actively-pursued small-molecule pocket in the human ortholog (chemical probes exist), which is unusual for PDZ domains generally (most PDZ domains are considered difficult/shallow). This is a protein-protein-interaction site, not a classic enzyme active site, so standard Vina-style docking against a rigid pocket may under-perform relative to fragment/peptidomimetic approaches used in the human PICK1 literature — worth flagging as a different docking strategy problem, not just a pocket-location problem.

A0A0C9RXK7.family: Tetraspanin (TM4SF) superfamily; IPR000301 (Tetraspanin, animals), IPR008952 (EC2 domain superfamily), IPR018499 (Tetraspanin/Peripherin). Pfam PF00335.

Q8T9S3.family: TCTP/Mss4-like family; IPR011057 (Mss4-like superfamily), IPR011323 (Mss4/TCTP), IPR018103 (TCTP conserved site), IPR018105 (TCTP family), IPR034737 (TCTP domain). Pfam PF00838 (TCTP).
Q8T9S3.oligomeric_state: MONOMER by default, with a documented DIMERIZATION-dependent activation mode
Q8T9S3.oligomeric_evidence: No SUBUNIT text for this specific tick accession. Human TCTP literature (not this accession) shows the calcium-binding, apoptosis/growth-regulation-relevant form is monomeric (solution structure PDB 2HR9 determined by NMR, described as having a rigid core with a flexible loop, consistent with a monomer), but a separate line of evidence shows dimerization is 'essential for TCTP's cytokine-like activity' in an allergic-response context, and that dimerization specifically requires an N-terminally truncated form (full-length TCTP does not readily dimerize via disulfide bonds the way the truncated form does). Net picture: default form monomeric; a specific truncated/activated form dimerizes for a specific extracellular signaling function.
Q8T9S3.binding_site_location: UNKNOWN as a defined druggable small-molecule pocket in the classic sense. TCTP is primarily characterized as a protein-protein-interaction hub (documented interactions include the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1, with published structural work on 'Structural transitions in TCTP tumor protein upon binding to the anti-apoptotic protein family member Mcl-1') and a Ca2+-binding protein (NMR-mapped Ca2+ site in 2HR9), rather than an enzyme with a catalytic cavity. The H2-H3 helix region has documented structural similarity to the H5-H6 helices of the apoptosis regulator Bax, which is itself a protein-interaction/membrane-insertion surface, not a small-molecule pocket.
Q8T9S3.site_residues_known: Not extracted to residue numbers here; the Ca2+-binding site was mapped by NMR in human TCTP (2HR9) but specific residues were not pulled in this pass.
Q8T9S3.characterized_relatives: Human TCTP: crystal structure PDB 1YZ1 (2.0 Å), solution/NMR structure PDB 2HR9. Parasite orthologs with solved structures: Plasmodium falciparum TCTP, PDB 3P3K; Plasmodium knowlesi TCTP, PDB 1TXJ. None of these are described in the sources reviewed here as being crystallized WITH a small-molecule drug-like ligand bound (Ca2+ and protein-partner peptides are the documented ligands, not drug-like small molecules) — so despite good structural coverage, this family lacks a directly transferable small-molecule-bound template.

Q8T9S3.druggability_note: Structurally well characterized (multiple PDB entries, including a parasite ortholog which is directly relevant precedent for anti-parasitic/vector-control drug discovery against this exact protein family) but functionally a protein-protein-interaction and Ca2+-sensing hub rather than an enzyme with an obvious catalytic pocket — expect this to behave more like the PICK1 (A0A0C9R1D7) entry in this chunk (surface-patch/PPI docking problem) than like the cathepsins or GST (classic enclosed-pocket enzymes).
